tileEnv.SH_FIXTURE_DESC: Sinclair ZX81 (1981) at its own untouched power-on screen: a white field with a single inverse-video K in the bottom-left corner and nothing else — no banner, no memory count, no copyright line. K is the machine telling you it is in keyword mode, where one keypress enters a whole BASIC word (P gives PRINT). MAME 0.289 zx81 with -bios 2nd and -ramsize 1K, drawn fullscreen with aspect correction on the bridge kiosk's 1024x768 X root, which is exactly the 4:3 of the television the machine was sold to be plugged into. Keyboard-only exhibit; no pointer device; the ZX81 has no sound hardware, so the AC97 stream is silent by design.

museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 12 kiosk runs MAME 0.289 (SUBTARGET=zx81, pinned upstream commit f34f0250, built in the Bookworm chroot by scripts/build-guests/emulators/build-mame-zx81.sh); streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other bridge tile. The ROM is the second revision (-bios 2nd, zx81a.rom, sha1 7b143ee9…), which is what almost every shipped ZX81 contained; it is preservation-source material copyright Nine Tiles Networks Ltd, staged on the box and never committed. RAM is pinned to the machine as sold, -ramsize 1K, rather than MAME's 16K default. The golden is the untouched power-on screen — a white field with one inverse K — and readiness is decided GEOMETRICALLY, not by counting bright pixels, because this machine blanks its display while it computes and a photometric test cannot tell that frame from the fixture. Keyboard-only exhibit; the ZX81 has no sound hardware. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/zx81.md.

reset.fixture: Sinclair ZX81 power-on screen: an empty white field with a single inverse-video K cursor in the bottom-left of the 32×24 grid, drawn fullscreen by MAME 0.289 zx81 (-bios 2nd, -ramsize 1K) on the kiosk's 1024x768 X root. The golden INTERNAL snapshot restores that untouched cold boot; no post-restore keys. Baking anything else was never on the table — this machine prints no banner at all, so its power-on screen is the only state that is unambiguously the machine's own rather than a previous visitor's. Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); AC97 audio is present but silent, because the ZX81 had no sound hardware.
